findings.description: Critical: `openspec/schemas/provider-model-map.schema.json` remains v2 provider→single `tierEntry` and is cited as the contract for agent-archetypes.3/4, but D14 plus skill-workflow.3 require exact agent-harness + dispatch-kind ordered ModelSpec chains (arrays), which today's schema cannot express—and live configs already need distinct CLI vs SDK chains (e.g. claude-remote, codex-remote).
findings.resolution: Version the provider-model-map (or archetypes model-policy) schema to require per-(agent_id|harness, dispatch_kind, tier) non-empty ordered ModelSpec arrays; update change-context contract refs and task 4.8 acceptance to validate the new shape, including distinct CLI/SDK identifiers.

findings.description: Critical: Tasks 4.7–4.9 characterize, re-resolve, and delete `agents.yaml` model/`model_fallbacks` fields, but no requirement or task SHALL migrate/seed those existing primary+fallback values into the new `archetypes.yaml` per-(agent, dispatch_kind) chains before removal—so flag-off / pre-change parity (agent-archetypes.1, model-routing.14) has no data-migration owner.
findings.resolution: Add an explicit migration step (and scenario) that copies each agent's current CLI/SDK model + model_fallbacks into ordered archetypes chains, asserts behavioral parity, then allows field removal in 4.9.

findings.description: Critical: When `ROUTING_ADAPTIVE` is on, OpenAPI `select_model` returns a single `Candidate` plus scored `alternatives` (no thinking, no ordered capacity chain), while agent-archetypes.4 / skill-workflow.2 require capacity retries to advance only within the harness+dispatch-kind `ModelSpec` chain from `archetypes.yaml`—the plan never defines how adaptive primary selection composes with that static capacity chain.
findings.resolution: Specify composition: e.g. adaptive may replace only the primary ModelSpec while retaining the route's static ordered fallbacks; or return a full ModelSpec chain; or re-resolve on capacity. Reflect the chosen rule in OpenAPI (thinking + chain) and in agent-archetypes/model-routing scenarios.

findings.description: Critical: Task 3.10 implements `ROUTING_ADAPTIVE` delegation with D2's archetypes-owned static fallback before tasks 4.7–4.9 create harness-aware chains and remove agents.yaml models (4.7 even depends on 3.11→3.10). Until ownership lands, 3.10 either contradicts D14/D2 by still reading agents.yaml/ambient defaults, or depends on chains that do not yet exist.
findings.resolution: Reorder or split: land harness-aware archetypes chain loading + data migration before enabling D2 fallback semantics in 3.10, or amend 3.9–3.10 to preserve current dual-source static behavior until 4.9 flips the sole-source invariant.

findings.description: Nit: `SelectModelRequest` omits `agent_id` / `dispatch_kind` (and `Candidate` omits thinking), yet D14 static fallback and discovery injection are harness- and dispatch-kind-specific; without these fields the HTTP/MCP select path cannot return a correctly scoped archetypes chain or preserve thinking levels.
findings.resolution: Extend SelectModelRequest with required or conditionally required agent/dispatch context and extend Candidate (or add ModelSpec/chain fields) to carry thinking and ordered fallbacks used on capacity errors.

findings.description: Nit: Tasks 4.8–4.9 and wp-model-config-ownership require migrating discovery, coordination-bridge, and vendor_health off agents.yaml models, but skill-workflow/agent-archetypes only state negative constraints (no models in agents.yaml)—there is no SHALL that discovery/bridge responses expose the resolved archetypes chain or that health reporting must not invent ambient models.
findings.resolution: Add MODIFIED/ADDED scenarios for get_dispatch_configs / HTTP / MCP / bridge payloads including the resolved ordered chain, and for vendor_health reading that chain (or omitting models) without ambient defaults.

findings.description: Nit: `wp-probes` description/title still say tasks 6.1–6.6 while write_allow and tasks include 6.7–6.8 quota probe, and verification `-k 'probes or tripwires'` will not match `test_quota*`.
findings.resolution: Update package description to tasks 6.1–6.8 and extend the pytest -k expression to include quota (or run the quota test path explicitly).

findings.description: Nit: agent-archetypes.1 and model-routing.14 say flag-off must equal/restore “pre-change” static behavior, which conflicts with the intentional BREAKING storage move unless read as behavioral equivalence after migrating chains into archetypes.yaml.
findings.resolution: Reword scenarios to require equivalent selected ModelSpec chains (and capacity order) to the pre-migration agents.yaml+aliases composition, not identical storage or code paths.

findings.description: Optional: Cross-file missing-route / orphan-harness validation failures are required to fail before dispatch, but no requirement emits a structured signal/metric for those configuration errors (unlike resolver timeout fallback).
findings.resolution: Optionally require an audit/OTel signal when config validation rejects missing or orphan model routes so operators can detect misconfigured archetypes.yaml in fleet logs.

findings.description: FYI: D13’s optional quota-axi path shells out via `npx -y quota-axi` against local provider credentials; the plan correctly marks it read-only and off-by-default, but implementers should pin/verify the package and keep credentials out of argv/logs.
findings.resolution: During wp-probes implementation, pin the quota-axi version, document the trust boundary, and ensure subprocess output redaction in tests.

findings.description: The D14 split is coherent: agents.yaml keeps harness mechanics including model_flag, archetypes.yaml owns curated ModelSpec chains, adaptive catalog stays dynamic-only, and wp-model-config-ownership is correctly serialized behind wp-resolver and wp-dispatch with non-overlapping parallel lanes elsewhere.
findings.resolution: Retain the ownership boundary and package sequencing while fixing the schema, data-migration, and adaptive/capacity composition gaps above.

findings.description: The 4.7→4.8→4.9 test-first sequence (characterize sync/async/SDK/discovery/health, then versioned resolution, then remove legacy fields and ambient defaults) is the right migration shape for eliminating dual model authorities without a big-bang cutover.
findings.resolution: Keep the three-step order; insert the explicit agents.yaml→archetypes.yaml data-migration assertion between 4.8 and 4.9.

findings.description: Fallback resilience is well specified at the control-plane layer: ROUTING_ADAPTIVE default off, >2s/error fallback, additive migrations, metered ceiling fallback to subscription/local, and quota probe degrade-to-reactive.
findings.resolution: Keep these degrade paths; ensure the static fallback target after D14 is always a validated archetypes chain rather than ambient harness defaults.
